prompt.en: According to the passage, Tabatabai reads the whole surah as a statement of the three roots of religion, and it begins with prophethood.

prompt.en: According to Imam al-Sadiq, what does the name Ya Seen mean?

options.en: O bearer of the Wise Quran

explanation.en: Asked what Yaseen means, Imam al-Sadiq said it is a name of the Prophet and its meaning is 'O hearer of the revelation.'

anchor.quote: A name from the names of the Prophet, and its meaning is: O hearer of the revelation

prompt.en: "The word has certainly become due against most of them - those who do not affirm the wilaya of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams after him." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq glossed the verse, saying the word has become due against those who do not affirm the wilaya of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams after him.

anchor.quote: The word has certainly become due against most of them - those who do not affirm the wilaya of Amir al-Mu'minin and the Imams after him

prompt.en: Tusi cautions that God has not literally chained the disbeliever, that this is a ____, as elsewhere the Quran speaks of deafness in the ears.

explanation.en: Tusi reads the iron collars not as literal chains but as a likeness, the way the Quran elsewhere speaks of deafness in the ears.

anchor.quote: Tusi cautions that God has not literally chained the disbeliever, that this is a likeness, as elsewhere the Quran speaks of deafness in the ears

prompt.en: According to the perspectives, what reading of the manifest Imam do both traditions share?

options.en: The straight path the Prophet was sent upon
The good news of forgiveness and a noble reward
The barrier before and behind the faithless

explanation.en: The perspectives note that the Shia commentators give the same gloss as al-Tabari, both reading the manifest Imam as a preserved record, before the Shia reports add Amir al-Mu'minin.

anchor.quote: The Shia commentators give the same gloss of a preserved record

prompt.en: Tabatabai notes that such people still acknowledged God, yet held that He had entrusted the world's running to His ____.

explanation.en: The essay explains that these townspeople still acknowledged God, yet held that He had handed the running of the world to His nearer creatures, so they rejected the human messengers.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai notes that such people still acknowledged God, yet held that He had entrusted the world's running to His nearer creatures

prompt.en: In verse 18 the town calls the messengers a bad omen. How does the passage explain this kind of ill omen?

options.en: An omen the people draw from their prophets
An omen the prophets draw from the people
A curse the prophets laid upon the town
A warning the messengers took from bad signs

explanation.en: The note explains that the ill omen in this verse is the one people draw from their prophets, not one the prophets draw, as the town did when it called its messengers a bad omen.

anchor.quote: the ill omen here is the one people draw from their prophets, not one the prophets draw

prompt.en: "There are three things from which no prophet, nor anyone below him, was left immune: ill omen, envy, and pondering the whisperings about creation." Who said this?

explanation.en: Imam al-Sadiq taught that no prophet, nor anyone below him, is immune from three things: ill omen, envy, and pondering the whisperings about creation.

anchor.quote: There are three things from which no prophet, nor anyone below him, was left immune: ill omen, envy, and pondering the whisperings about creation

prompt.en: According to the essay, why does Tabatabai say the man worshipped God?

Out of fear of the Fire
Because God is worthy of worship
To become one of the honoured ones

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai dwells on the man's faith: he worshipped not from hope of paradise or fear of the Fire, but because God is worthy of worship.

anchor.quote: he worshipped not from hope of paradise or fear of the Fire but because God is worthy of worship

prompt.en: According to the passage, the paradise the believing man was told to enter is the final Paradise of the resurrection.

explanation.en: The essay says Tabatabai holds the man's people had killed him and that the paradise he entered is that of the barzakh, the intermediate life, not the final resurrection.

anchor.quote: that the paradise he entered is that of the barzakh, and reads the verse as evidence for that intermediate life

prompt.en: Tabatabai reads them as signs of creation and governance pointing to His ____ alone.

prompt.en: "The drop falls from the sky to the earth upon the plants, the fruit and the trees; people and cattle eat of it." Who said this?

anchor.quote: The drop falls from the sky to the earth upon the plants, the fruit and the trees

prompt.en: According to the narration on verse 40, what are the sun and the moon called?

options.en: Two lights that share one orbit by turns
The sun, which lends its light to the moon
The authority of the day and the authority of the night
Rulers whose turns the night will one day reverse

explanation.en: The narration names the sun the authority of the day and the moon the authority of the night, so neither crowds into the other's time.

anchor.quote: The sun is the authority of the day and the moon the authority of the night

prompt.en: The commentary explains 'that which is before you' as sins and 'that which is behind you' as their punishment.

explanation.en: The narration glosses the warning as sins that are before you and the punishment that is behind you, so restating it that way is true.

anchor.quote: beware of that which is before you, of sins, and of that which is behind you, of punishment

prompt.en: In the essay's closing, what does Tabatabai identify the single Cry as?

The cry of those drowning in the laden ship
The believers' call to spend in God's path
The first blast of the trumpet, opening the Return

anchor.quote: Tabatabai identifies this Cry as the first blast of the trumpet, opening his account of the Return

prompt.en: How does Tabatabai explain that no soul is wronged in the judgment?

options.en: The recompense is the deeds themselves
Every sin is forgiven at the Trumpet blast
The apostles intercede for every soul
The guilty are offered a second chance

explanation.en: The essay says the recompense being the deeds themselves is the very proof that no wrong is done, since each soul meets only what it used to do.

anchor.quote: Tabatabai notes that the recompense being the deeds themselves is the very proof that no wrong is done

prompt.en: The couches are the thrones with the bridal ____ over them.

explanation.en: Asked about the couches of paradise, Imam al-Baqir glosses them as thrones with bridal canopies raised over them, so the missing word is canopies.

anchor.quote: The couches are the thrones with the bridal canopies over them.

prompt.en: According to al-Qummi's note on the summons 'Get apart', what does all creation beg for as it stands sweating?

To be brought to account, even to the Fire
To be shown mercy and spared
To be sent back to the world to repent

explanation.en: In al-Qummi's picture the terror is so great that all creation, bridled by its own sweat, begs to be brought to account even if that means the Fire.

anchor.quote: all creation left standing until sweat bridles them, crying, 'Lord, bring us to account, even to the Fire,'

prompt.en: The passage treats the weakening that comes with old age as a refutation of those who say nature, food and the heavens alone shape a person.

anchor.quote: al-Qummi reads this verse as a refutation of the materialists who deny God's oneness, holding that man is formed by nature, food and the turning of the heavens

prompt.en: al-Tabrisi takes the ____ as a plain proof of the Lord who provides.

prompt.en: "How utterly astonishing is the one who denies death while he sees people dying every day and night." Who said this?

anchor.quote: How utterly astonishing is the one who denies death while he sees people dying every day and night

prompt.en: In the essay's closing movement, how does the passage answer the man who asks who can revive bones once they have decayed?

The Prophet is told to grieve over the question
The deniers are left to answer it themselves

explanation.en: The essay says the answer comes at once, that the One who produced the bones the first time and knows every creature will raise them again.

anchor.quote: The answer comes at once: the One who produced them first knows every creature
